newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil lower house to vote on oil bill Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Brazil lower house to vote on oil bill Wednesday.

text.p: A bill opening up Brazil's petroleum industry faces a full vote in the Chamber of Deputies Wednesday after the lower house approved Tuesday a motion giving the legislation priority treatment, officials said.

The Chamber of Deputies approved the motion with 287 members voting in favor, 113 against and four abstaining. For approval, the bill requires a simple majority of the lower house. It also needs to pass through the Senate.
The government wants the oil and gas bill through the lower house this week to clear the path for a first vote next week on its civil service reform bill.
Earlier Tuesday, a committee in the Chamber of Deputies approved the petroleum bill after months of discussions.
The legislation would allow private companies to compete or enter joint-ventures with state oil and gas giant Petrobras.
It would also create a new sector regulator, the National Petroleum Agency (ANP), and end fuel price subsidies within three years.

Government-allied lawmakers said they intended to present several amendments to the bill. One change proposed by the Liberal Front Party would strike down a clause which obliges the government to keep its controlling stake in Petrobras.
Another controversial amendment would eliminate an article of the bill that sets down criteria for the distribution of fuel and natural gas.
As it stands, the bill would allow producers of fuel and natural gas to sell directly to steelmakers, chemical and petrochemical companies and thermoelectric power plants.

All other fuel distribution would be conducted exclusively through licensed distributors, an idea which has met with opposition from government and oppostion quarters alike. Critics of the article say it would thwart competition and add to the cost of fuel in Brazil.
